doc.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Multi-track studio takes versus live jazz
summary: Ellis says live jazz is fun and nerve-wracking, and a mistake can be turned into a symphony.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: You know in the studios if they’re doing a multi-track recording, sometimes you get four or five chances at it.
How is that different from playing a night club where it’s your turn to solo and that’s it? The audience gets what you give that night.

You mean in a jazz situation? Oh well first of all that’s a lot of fun. I mean it can be a little nerve wracking if you’re doing a big concert you know. But jazz players, they just love that. It’s just what we do you know. And I know that we can make a mistake and turn it into a symphony, you know? That’s what you have to learn to do.
